entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Adam Smith?
entries.text: Adam Smith (baptise date 16 June 1723 – 17 July 1790) was a Scottish economist, who is called the Father of Modern Economics. He wrote two classic books, The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759) and An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776).
entries.title: Adam Smith

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Muhammad?
entries.text: Muhammad (Arabic: مُحَمَّدٌ; 570 – 8 June 632) was an Arab religious, social, and political leader, best known as the founder of Islam. Islamic teachings say Muhammad was a prophet who God inspired to preach and confirm the monotheistic teachings of Adam, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets.
entries.title: Muhammad

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Jawaharlal Nehru?
entries.text: Jawaharlal Nehru (also referred to as Pandit Nehru) (November 14, 1889 - May 27, 1964) was the first prime minister of India for 17 years. He became prime minister after India became independent in 1947.
entries.title: Jawaharlal Nehru

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Michael Faraday?
entries.text: Michael Faraday (Newington Butts, Surrey. 22 September 1791 – Hampton Court, Surrey, 25 August 1867) was the son of a blacksmith who became one of the most famous scientists of the 19th century.
entries.title: Michael Faraday

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was David Hilbert?
entries.text: David Hilbert (Königsberg, Prussia, 23 January 1862 –Göttingen, Germany, 14 February 1943) was a German mathematician, logician, and philosopher of mathematics. He is widely considered to be one of the most influential and greatest mathematicians of the 19th and 20th centuries.
entries.title: David Hilbert

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Joseph Haydn?
entries.text: Franz Joseph Haydn (31 March 1732 – 31 May 1809) was an Austrian composer. He was one of the most famous composers in the Classical music period.
entries.title: Joseph Haydn

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Charlie Chaplin?
entries.text: Sir Charles Spencer "Charlie" Chaplin (16 April 1889 – 25 December 1977) was an English comic actor, filmmaker, and composer. He was famous in silent movies (where there was no talking or sound).
entries.title: Charlie Chaplin

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Abu Nuwas?
entries.text: Abū Nuwās al-Ḥasan ibn Hānī al-Ḥakamī (variant: Al-Ḥasan ibn Hānī 'Abd al-Awal al-Ṣabāḥ, Abū 'Alī (الحسن بن هانئ بن عبد الأول بن الصباح ،ِابو علي), known as Abū Nuwās al-Salamī (أبو نواس السلمي) or just Abū Nuwās (أبو نواس Abū Novās); c. 756 – c. 814) was a classical Arabic poet. He was born in Persia.
entries.title: Abu Nuwas

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Yuri Gagarin?
entries.text: Yuri Alexeyevich Gagarin (Russian: Юрий Алексеевич Гагарин; March 9, 1934 – March 27, 1968) was a Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (astronaut). He was the first person to travel into space.
entries.title: Yuri Gagarin

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Materialism?
entries.text: Materialism is the philosophical belief that the world is made of material, and that there are no other types of entity (things). Everything is composed of material.
entries.title: Materialism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Civilization?
entries.text: Civilization (or civilisation) comes from the Latin word civis meaning someone who lives in a city. The Romans usually wanted conquered people to live in towns.
entries.title: Civilization

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Thought?
entries.text: Thought is the operation of the brain in conscious activity. It may or may not be goal-directed, aimed at solving specific problems.
entries.title: Thought

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Phoneme?
entries.text: Phonemes are the units of sound (speech) that distinguish one word from another in a particular language. Most varieties (accents and dialects) of spoken English have about 23 consonant phonemes and 21 vowel phonemes (altogether 44 phonemes) but only 26 letters in writing.
entries.title: Phoneme

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Year?
entries.text: The year (symbol: y or a, also known as the annum or annus) is about 365 days (except in a leap year). It is the time it takes the Earth to go completely around (orbit) the sun once.
entries.title: Year

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Shark?
entries.text: Sharks are a superorder of fish. This superorder is also known by its scientific name Selachimorpha.
entries.title: Shark

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Domestic sheep?
entries.text: A domestic sheep (Ovis aries) is a domesticated mammal related to wild sheep and goats. Sheep are owned and looked after by a sheep farmer.
entries.title: Domestic sheep

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Flower?
entries.text: A flower is the reproductive part of flowering plants. Flowers are also called the bloom or blossom of a plant.
entries.title: Flower

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Deafness?
entries.text: Deafness is when someone cannot hear at all, or cannot hear well. Deafness is also known as 'hearing loss'.
entries.title: Deafness

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Plate tectonics?
entries.text: Plate tectonics is a theory of geology. It explains movement of the Earth's lithosphere.
entries.title: Plate tectonics

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Force?
entries.text: In physics, a force is a push or pull or a twist between objects. It is called an interaction because if one object acts on another, its action is matched by a reaction from the other object.
entries.title: Force

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Metal?
entries.text: Some chemical elements are called metals. Most elements in the periodic table are metals.
entries.title: Metal

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Quantum mechanics?
entries.text: Quantum mechanics explains how the universe works with things that are even smaller than atoms. It is also called quantum physics or quantum theory.
entries.title: Quantum mechanics

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Geometry?
entries.text: Geometry (from Ancient Greek: Γεωμετρία (romanized: Geometria (English: "Land measurement") derived from Γη (romanized: Ge; English: "Earth" or "land") and also derived from Μέτρον) (romanized: Métron; English: "A measure")) is a branch of mathematics that studies the size, shapes, positions and dimensions of things.
entries.title: Geometry

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Maize?
entries.text: Maize or Indian corn (called corn in some countries) is Zea mays, a member of the grass family Poaceae. It is a cereal grain which was first grown by people in ancient Central America.
entries.title: Maize

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Citrus?
entries.text: Citrus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the rue family, Rutaceae.
entries.title: Citrus

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Meat?
entries.text: Meat is animal flesh which is used for food. Most often, it is used to describe skeletal muscles and fats that are found with it.
entries.title: Meat

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Table salt?
entries.text: Table salt is a mineral composed mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl). This is a chemical compound, one of many salts.
entries.title: Table salt

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Potato?
entries.text: A potato is a vegetable, the Solanum tuberosum. It is a small plant with big leaves.
entries.title: Potato

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Engineering?
entries.text: Engineering is the use of science and math to design or make things. People who do engineering are called engineers.
entries.title: Engineering

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Library?
entries.text: A library is a place where many books are kept. Most libraries are public and let people take the books to use in their home.
entries.title: Library

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Inductor?
entries.text: An inductor is an electrical device used in electrical circuits because it acts like inertia in the electrical circuit. Just like inertia opposes the change in state of motion, inductor opposes the change in electric current.
entries.title: Inductor

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Painting?
entries.text: Painting is using colors to make visual art. It is also the word for a painted work of art.
entries.title: Painting

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Canal?
entries.text: A canal is a waterway made by humans. For many centuries, canals have been built as a way of transporting heavy goods in barges or boats.
entries.title: Canal

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Hagia Sophia?
entries.text: Hagia Sophia (Greek: Ἁγία Σοφία, meaning the Holy Wisdom) is a mosque in the eastern Bosporus of Istanbul, Turkey. It was originally a Byzantine Eastern Orthodox cathedral and was turned into a mosque after the conquest of Constantinople by the Ottoman Empire.
entries.title: Hagia Sophia

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Rock music?
entries.text: Rock music is a genre of popular music. It developed in the late 1900s, chiefly in the United States.
entries.title: Rock music

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Bronze Age?
entries.text: The Bronze Age is a period in human prehistory when people made tools from bronze, an alloy (mixture) of metals.
entries.title: Bronze Age

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Prehistory?
entries.text: Prehistory (or better known as Pre-history) is the time before people began to write. It lasted from around 4.5 billion BC – 3000 BC, during the Stone Age.
entries.title: Prehistory

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Great Depression?
entries.text: The Great Depression was the global economic crisis that started after the U.S. stock market crash in 1929. The prices on the Wall Street stock market greatly fell from October 24 to 29, 1929.
entries.title: Great Depression

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is North Pole?
entries.text: The North Pole is the point that is farthest north on Earth. It is the point on which axis of Earth turns.
entries.title: North Pole

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is North America?
entries.text: North America is a large continent in the Northern and Western Hemispheres of Earth. It is to the east of the Pacific Ocean, the west of the Atlantic Ocean, the south of the Arctic Ocean, and it is the northern part of the Americas.
entries.title: North America

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is São Paulo?
entries.text: São Paulo (Portuguese for Saint Paul) is the capital of the Brazilian state of the same name. It is the most populous city city in Brazil, South America, and the Southern Hemisphere, and the second-most populous city in the Western Hemisphere, after Mexico City, Mexico.
entries.title: São Paulo

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Baltic Sea?
entries.text: The Baltic Sea is a sea in northern Europe between Scandinavia, Finland, Russia, the Baltic countries, Poland, and Germany.
entries.title: Baltic Sea

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Suez Canal?
entries.text: The Suez Canal (Arabic: قناة السويس, Qanā al-Suways, French: Le Canal de Suez) is a canal in Egypt. It lies west of the Sinai Peninsula.
entries.title: Suez Canal

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Circle of latitude?
entries.text: On the Earth, a circle of latitude is an imaginary east-west circle that connects all locations with a given latitude. A location's position along a circle of latitude is given by its longitude.
entries.title: Circle of latitude

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Mozambique Channel?
entries.text: The Mozambique Channel is a part of the Indian Ocean. Its between the Somali Sea to the north, the island nation of Madagascar in the east, and Mozambique in the west.
entries.title: Mozambique Channel

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Lake Maracaibo?
entries.text: Lake Maracaibo (Spanish: Lago de Maracaibo) is a large brackish tidal bay (or tidal estuary) in Venezuela. It is an "inlet of the Caribbean Sea".
entries.title: Lake Maracaibo

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Dili?
entries.text: Dili is the capital of the country East Timor. People from Portugal moved there around 1520.
entries.title: Dili

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Dushanbe?
entries.text: Dushanbe (Tajik: Душанбе, Persian: دوشنبه) is the capital city of Tajikistan. About 562,000 people live in Dushanbe as of 2000.
entries.title: Dushanbe

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Ho Chi Minh City?
entries.text: Ho Chi Minh City (Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh) is a city in southern Vietnam. It is governed as a municipality and includes a large rural area.
entries.title: Ho Chi Minh City

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Xi'an?
entries.text: Xi'an (Chinese: 西安 pinyin:Xī'ān) is the capital city of the Shaanxi Province in China. Its metropolitan area has a population of 6 million people in 2011.
entries.title: Xi'an

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Yangon?
entries.text: Yangon (Burmese: ရန်ကုန်မြို့) also known as Rangoon, is the largest city in Myanmar. It was also the capital city until 2006.
entries.title: Yangon

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Bissau?
entries.text: Bissau is the capital city of Guinea-Bissau. It is also the largest city in the country; around 355,000 people live there.
entries.title: Bissau

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Dallas?
entries.text: Dallas is a large city in the northern part of the U.S. state of Texas. It is a part of a much larger group of cities called the Metroplex, along with important cities like Arlington, Mansfield, Grand Prarie Denton, Fort Worth, and Plano.
entries.title: Dallas

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Toronto?
entries.text: Toronto is the capital city of the province of Ontario. It is found on the northwest side of Lake Ontario behind New York City and Chicago.
entries.title: Toronto

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Managua?
entries.text: Managua has been the capital city of Nicaragua since 1855. There had been an Indian settlement there before the Spanish, but the modern city was founded as Leal Villa de Santiago de Managua in 1811.
entries.title: Managua

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Barcelona?
entries.text: Barcelona is the capital city of Catalonia, which is a region of Spain. Barcelona is the largest city on the Mediterranean coast.
entries.title: Barcelona

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Ivory Coast?
entries.text: Ivory Coast or Côte d'Ivoire, officially the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, is a country in West Africa.
entries.title: Ivory Coast

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Cyprus?
entries.text: Cyprus (officially the Republic of Cyprus) is an island country in the Mediterranean Sea. Cyprus is in Asia, along with being apart of the Middle East and the Levant (but politically, part of modern Europe).
entries.title: Cyprus

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Denmark?
entries.text: Denmark (Danish: Danmark), officially named the Kingdom of Denmark, is a Nordic country in Northern Europe. It is the furthest south of the Scandinavian countries, to the northeast of North America, to the south of Norway and south-west of Sweden (which it is connected to by a bridge).
entries.title: Denmark

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Lesotho?
entries.text: Lesotho is a small country in southern Africa. It is entirely surrounded by South Africa.
entries.title: Lesotho

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Liberia?
entries.text: The Republic of Liberia is a small country on the coast of West Africa. It has common borders with Sierra Leone, Guinea, and Ivory Coast.
entries.title: Liberia

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Samoa?
entries.text: The Independent State of Samoa is a country in the Pacific Ocean. It became independent from New Zealand in 1962.
entries.title: Samoa

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Sierra Leone?
entries.text: Sierra Leone is a country in West Africa. Its capital is Freetown.
entries.title: Sierra Leone

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Byte?
entries.text: The byte (symbol: B or o, also known as the octet) is a unit of measurement of the size of information on a computer or other electronic device. A single byte is eight bits.
entries.title: Byte

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Event horizon?
entries.text: In general relativity, an event horizon is the part of a black hole where light cannot escape. Imagine the black hole to be like a ball that you could see in a large spot of emptiness.
entries.title: Event horizon

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Sundial?
entries.text: A sundial shows the current solar time during the day. It does this because the sun appears to move through the sky.
entries.title: Sundial

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Celestial coordinate system?
entries.text: A celestial coordinate system is a coordinate system that helps astronomers specify the location of objects in the sky. These objects may be stars, planets or even satellites.
entries.title: Celestial coordinate system

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Asteroid belt?
entries.text: The asteroid belt or main belt is a ring of small and large rocks and dust between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. The biggest object in the asteroid belt is Ceres, a dwarf planet.
entries.title: Asteroid belt

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Haumea?
entries.text: 136108 Haumea (symbol ) is a dwarf planet in the Solar System. Its discovery was announced in 2005 by astronomers Michael E. Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz of the United States, and J. L. Ortiz of Spain.
entries.title: Haumea (dwarf planet)

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Altair?
entries.text: Altair, also called α Aquilae, α Aql, is the brightest star in the constellation of Aquila.
entries.title: Altair

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Star cluster?
entries.text: A star cluster is a group of stars. They are held together by mutual gravitation.
entries.title: Star cluster

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Galaxy morphological classification?
entries.text: Galaxy morphological classification is a system used by astronomers to divide galaxies into groups based on how they look.
entries.title: Galaxy morphological classification

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Observable universe?
entries.text: In Big Bang cosmology, the observable universe is what, in theory, can be seen from Earth. That is light, or other signals, which has had time to reach the Earth since the beginning of the cosmological expansion.
entries.title: Observable universe

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Habitable zone?
entries.text: A habitable zone (HZ) in astronomy is a region of space where conditions are best for life to form as on Earth. Planets in these areas are the most likely to have extraterrestrial life.
entries.title: Habitable zone

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Red giant?
entries.text: A red giant is a giant star that has the mass of about one-half to ten times the mass of our Sun. Red giants get their name because they appear to be colored red and they are very large.
entries.title: Red giant

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Stellar nucleosynthesis?
entries.text: Stellar nucleosynthesis is the creation (nucleosynthesis) of chemical elements by nuclear fusion reactions in stars. This fusion reaction also creates the stars' light and heat.
entries.title: Stellar nucleosynthesis

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Lunar eclipse?
entries.text: A lunar eclipse is an astronomical phenomenon. It happens when the moon passes through the shadow of the Earth.
entries.title: Lunar eclipse

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Potential energy?
entries.text: Potential energy is the stored or pent-up energy of an object. It is often contrasted with kinetic energy.
entries.title: Potential energy

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Free fall?
entries.text: Free fall is what happens when an object is let to fall on its own without propulsion or resistance. Someone who is standing is not in free fall, but someone jumping from an aeroplane is, until air resistance builds up, ending in terminal velocity.
entries.title: Free fall

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Angstrom?
entries.text: An angstrom or ångström (symbol Å) is a unit of length that equals 0.1 nanometer (nm). It can be written in scientific notation as 1×10−10 m (normalized notation) or 1 E-10 m (exponential notation) — both mean 1/10,000,000,000 meters.
entries.title: Angstrom

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Fluid dynamics?
entries.text: Fluid dynamics is the motion of fluids (liquids and gases). It is one of the oldest studies of physics.
entries.title: Fluid dynamics

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Doppler effect?
entries.text: The Doppler effect is a change in frequency and wavelength of a wave. It is caused by the change in distance between the thing creating the wave (causer) and whatever is measuring seeing or hearing the wave (watcher or observer).
entries.title: Doppler effect

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Wavelength?
entries.text: A wavelength is the length of the shortest repeating part of a "sine wave". All waves can be formed by adding up sine waves.
entries.title: Wavelength

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Celsius?
entries.text: Celsius (more precisely, a degree Celsius), sometimes called centigrade, is a unit of measurement that is used in most countries to measure temperature. The unit was created by Anders Celsius (1701–1744), a Swedish astronomer.
entries.title: Celsius

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Kelvin?
entries.text: The Kelvin scale (symbol: K) is the SI unit of temperature. It is named in honour of the physicist William Thomson, the first Lord Kelvin (1824–1907).
entries.title: Kelvin

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Blackbody radiation?
entries.text: Blackbody radiation is radiation produced by heated objects, particularly from a blackbody. A blackbody is an object that absorbs all radiation (visible light, infrared light, ultraviolet light, etc.) that falls on it.
entries.title: Blackbody radiation

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Magnetic flux?
entries.text: Magnetic flux is a measure of the magnetic field lines passing through a surface, such as a loop of wire. The magnetic flux through a closed surface such as a sphere is always zero, because the magnetic field lines going into the closed surface are balanced by field lines coming out.
entries.title: Magnetic flux
